subject: Marketplace Private Offer Unit Price Qualification (AWS/GCP/Azure)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>, AWS Marketplace - Partner Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>, GCP Partners <gcp-partner@google.com>, Azure Marketplace <azure-marketplace@microsoft.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace Private Offer Unit Price Qualification (AWS/GCP/Azure) — post-call recap

Thanks everyone for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on pricing inputs for the private offers across marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure).

Call summary (BrightCart + marketplaces):
- BrightCart shared expected volume profile: 50M tokens/mo initial pilot (3 months), scaling to 200M tokens/mo within 12 months.
- BrightCart expects marketplace billing via private offers (they prefer marketplace invoicing for procurement).
- Primary question: what gross unit price should we list in each marketplace private offer so BrightCart receives a target economics of ~$1,000 per 1M tokens? (BrightCart gave target range $900–$1,200 / 1M tokens).

Redwood internal baseline (shared on call):
- Target net revenue to Redwood (post-marketplace fee): ~$750 per 1M tokens to meet established unit economics for BrightCart workload (model family: rwd-large-8k, quantized).
- Marketplace fee assumptions to validate: AWS ~18%, GCP ~20%, Azure ~22% (we need marketplace confirmation).

What we need from marketplace reps / procurement:
1) Confirm the marketplace fee % that will be applied to private offers (listing + transaction fees).
2) Confirm whether marketplaces require gross-listed prices or accept net pricing with marketplace fee layering.
3) Any marketplace minimums or rounding rules for unit price (e.g., per-1M token SKU granularity, currency rounding).

Proposed gross price mapping (starting point - please validate):
- Redwood target net: $750 / 1M tokens
- AWS gross = $750 / (1 - 0.18) ≈ $915 / 1M tokens
- GCP gross = $750 / (1 - 0.20) = $938 / 1M tokens
- Azure gross = $750 / (1 - 0.22) ≈ $962 / 1M tokens

Attachments: pricing sheet (private_offer_pricing_sheet.xlsx) with row-level math and monthly spend examples for 50M/200M tokens.

Next steps (owners):
- AWS rep: confirm fee % and any listing constraints (action: AWS rep) — by EOD Thu 3/31
- GCP rep: confirm fee % and rounding rules (action: GCP rep) — by EOD Thu 3/31
- Azure rep: confirm fee % and private offer flow (action: Azure rep) — by EOD Thu 3/31
- Rafael/Aditya: prepare final gross price table and marketplace-ready private offer attachments once fee numbers confirmed (action: Rafael/Aditya) — by Fri 4/1

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: AWS Marketplace - Partner Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace Private Offer Unit Price Qualification (AWS/GCP/Azure) — AWS fees

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa. Confirming on AWS Marketplace side:
- Applicable fee for private offers + transaction processing is 18% on gross listed price (this is the % we apply to the invoice amount).
- Private offers can be listed per-1M token SKU, USD, and we allow granular pricing to the dollar (no additional hidden rounding).
- AWS prefers gross-listed prices (we invoice the customer the gross; partners receive payout net of the fee).

Given Redwood's net target of $750 / 1M tokens, the gross to list on AWS to meet that net is indeed approximately $915 / 1M tokens.

A couple of notes/questions from our procurement team:
- Do you plan to include any marketplace credit/promotions? Those are typically applied as separate promotions and don't change fee calc but do affect customer payables.
- Please confirm whether BrightCart requires monthly or annual billing cadence for the private offer — that affects invoice terms.

Happy to do a short follow-up to validate the private offer draft once you send the listings.

— AWS Marketplace Team
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace - Partner Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>, GCP Partners <gcp-partner@google.com>, Azure Marketplace <azure-marketplace@microsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace Private Offer Unit Price Qualification (AWS/GCP/Azure) — proposed mapping and economics

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. I ran the numbers in the attached pricing sheet and added monthly spend examples for BrightCart volumes. Key calls: 
- Confirmed marketplace fees (AWS 18% / GCP 20% / Azure 22%) as starting assumptions. If any marketplace rep updates those, we'll re-run.
- Recommended gross list prices (rounded to whole dollars for SKU simplicity):
  - AWS: $915 / 1M tokens
  - GCP: $938 / 1M tokens
  - Azure: $962 / 1M tokens

Example customer economics (50M tokens/mo pilot):
- Listed AWS gross @ $915 => customer monthly = $45,750; Redwood net ≈ $37,515 after 18% fee.
- If BrightCart wants a target spend cap: we included a table showing how to structure a tiered private offer (pilot discount -> steady-state pricing).

Open items for BrightCart/procurement:
1) Confirm target $/1M token within the $900–$1,200 range (BrightCart said $1,000 target on call). If they want $1,000 net instead of $750 net, we need to re-run mapping.
2) Confirm billing cadence and whether they require annual commit pricing in marketplace (that can materially change listed price and discount cadence).

Action: Marissa to confirm BrightCart's final target net $/1M (we assumed Redwood net $750 to meet our internal unit economics). Rafael/Aditya will stand by to produce final private offer docs once we have confirmations.

-Rafael
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace - Partner Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>, GCP Partners <gcp-partner@google.com>, Azure Marketplace <azure-marketplace@microsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace Private Offer Unit Price Qualification (AWS/GCP/Azure) — next steps

Thanks all — quick next steps to close this out: 
- BrightCart (procurement): please confirm by EOD Thu whether their target is $1,000 / 1M tokens gross or if they intended $1,000 as the customer-facing listed price (we need to know if $1,000 is net or gross). If they confirm $1,000 customer-facing, Redwood net drops to ~ $820 on AWS (with 18% fee) — that may compress our margin.
- Marketplaces: please confirm any dev-ops/integration steps we need to prepare for ingestion of private offer SKUs (doc templates attached).
- Rafael/Aditya: please prepare two versions of the private offer attachments: (A) net-to-Redwood target $750 / 1M mapping, and (B) customer-listed $1,000 / 1M mapping with resulting net to Redwood. Include tiered pricing rows for 0–50M, 50–200M, >200M tokens.

I've attached the pricing spreadsheet and our private offer template. Rafael/Aditya, I'll sync with you 10am PT tomorrow to finalize the docs for AWS/GCP/Azure.

Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: private_offer_pricing_sheet.xlsx (see tab: marketplace-mapping), marketplace_fee_breakdown.pdf, private_offer_template.docx
